verdict.rationale: Flagsmith has its own background automation. Release Pipelines move flags through stages automatically using triggers and actions, and can auto-generate change requests. Scheduled flags apply queued changes at a future time without anyone present. Both are limited to flag rollouts, and scheduled flags are one-off changes rather than recurring schedules. Running the MCP server inside a CI/CD pipeline relies on an external host, so it is not credited here. Missing for 10: general-purpose or recurring scheduled automations beyond flag changes, detail on trigger types and conditions, independent or hands-on confirmation that pipelines run autonomously.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Define stages that your flags progress through automatically, with triggers and actions that control rollouts to selected environments and audiences.
Release Pipelines act as your intelligent release assistant, automating your entire feature flag deployment process.
Release Pipelines can automatically generate change requests when promoting flags to production, eliminating manual effort and streamlining your deployment workflow.
Scheduled flags allow you to queue and automatically apply changes to feature flags at a specified future time, eliminating the need for manual intervention at the exact moment of change.
